title: ISSEN vs Babbel: Voice Conversation vs Fixed Syllabus
summary: Weighing Babbel against ISSEN for speaking practice? Compare lesson structure, accents, pricing, and fit before choosing in October 2026.
body_markdown:
Short daily lessons feel productive until you try to say something unscripted and nothing comes out. That's the moment most learners start looking beyond Babbel for a Babbel alternative for speaking that pushes them into real conversation. In this comparison, we'll walk through how Babbel's syllabus and new voice feature stack up against a real-time AI tutor, so you can tell which one matches where you are right now.


**TLDR:**


- Babbel runs a fixed syllabus across 14 languages with Babbel Speak scenarios; ISSEN runs open voice conversations across 60+ languages that adapt mid-turn.
- Babbel's AI-Enhanced Speech Recognition scores pronunciation inside vocabulary lessons; ISSEN keeps conversations uninterrupted and handles pronunciation in a separate Shadowing mode.
- Babbel builds separate tracks per language variant (Spanish Spain vs Mexico); ISSEN switches regional accents inside one track across Argentina, Mexico, Spain, and more.
- Babbel costs ~$8.95/month annually but caps you at lesson length; ISSEN runs $20-$29/month with unlimited daily reps, driving cost-per-conversation lower at daily volume.
- ISSEN suits B1+ learners pushing past the intermediate plateau (Swain, 1985) who need unpredictable speaking reps and cross-session memory, with a 10-minute free trial to start.


## What is Babbel


Babbel is a subscription language learning app offering structured lessons across 14 languages, with short vocabulary and grammar exercises. It added[Babbel Speak](https://www.babbel.com/press/en-us/releases/babbel-speak) , an AI-powered voice feature, in September 2025, alongside AI-Enhanced Speech Recognition.


## What is ISSEN


ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor covering 60+ languages, built around open-ended spoken conversation instead of locked lesson sequences. The tutor drives the exchange, adapts difficulty as you talk, and remembers context from previous sessions so you are not restarting from zero every time you open the app.


A few things worth knowing before the comparison:


- Voice-first design on iOS, Android, and web, with background mode for walks and commutes
- Multiple regional accents per language, including Spanish (Argentina, Mexico, Spain) and English (American, British, Australian)
- In-context flashcards tied to sentences you actually produced during conversation
- 10-minute free trial, then a flat monthly price with unlimited daily practice


ISSEN is one input inside a broader study plan, not a replacement for grammar instruction or real-world exposure, and understanding[how AI speaking practice works](https://www.issen.com/blog/how-ai-speaking-practice-works/) helps set expectations before you start.


## Lesson structure and learning methodology


Babbel organizes practice as a fixed syllabus of short lessons, roughly 10 to 15 minutes each, progressing through grammar explanations, vocabulary drills, and fill-in-the-blank exercises, a structure worth comparing against other[Speak alternatives](https://www.issen.com/blog/speak-competitors-alternatives/) built around conversation instead.[Babbel Speak](https://www.babbel.com/babbel-conversation-practice) layers AI voice scenarios on top, giving beginners preset dialogues to rehearse. If you want a defined path and visible daily progress, that structure works.


ISSEN runs differently. The tutor opens a conversation from the first session, picks a topic or lets you pick one, and adjusts vocabulary and pace inside a single turn as you speak. Mention your sister is visiting Lisbon next weekend and the tutor pivots to restaurant phrases for the trip. Shadowing lives in a separate mode for pronunciation drills, so conversation flow stays uninterrupted.


Babbel suits beginners who want a syllabus. ISSEN suits learners accumulating speaking reps to push past the intermediate plateau, where passive knowledge outpaces active production (Swain, 1985).


## Speaking practice and conversation features


Babbel Speak is a voice-led feature that walks learners through expert-curated real-life scenarios with scaffolded prompts, designed to help first-time learners go from silence to speech ([Babbel](https://www.babbel.com/press/en-us/releases/babbel-speak) ). AI-Enhanced Speech Recognition handles pronunciation feedback inside vocabulary lessons through repetition exercises. Babbel Live, the group-class offering with human instructors, was discontinued on July 1, 2025.


The practice happens inside preset situations: ordering at a cafe, checking in at a hotel, making small talk. You rehearse dialogues the app has written for you, which is useful for the first few hundred reps of spoken output.


ISSEN's open conversation mode runs without push-to-talk. Smart turn detection reads your pauses, so the tutor waits when you hesitate and responds quickly when you ask a question. Mid-conversation, the tutor pivots topics based on what you mention, adapts difficulty inside a single turn, and recalls what you stumbled over in earlier sessions, a pattern that also shows up among other[Speak app alternatives](https://www.issen.com/blog/speak-app-alternatives/) . Background and lock-screen mode keeps the conversation going while you walk the dog or ride the bus.


Babbel Speak fits beginners who want scenario rehearsal with guardrails. ISSEN fits learners who need unpredictable conversational pressure, the kind that surfaces gaps a scripted dialogue cannot.


## Pronunciation, accents, and feedback


Babbel's AI-Enhanced Speech Recognition sits inside vocabulary lessons, scoring your repetitions of individual words and short phrases with tailored feedback when you drift off target. Pronunciation work happens in the same session as grammar and vocab.


ISSEN splits the two. Voice conversations stay conversational, with no inline scoring interrupting the exchange.[Shadowing](https://www.issen.com/blog/shadowing-pronunciation-technique/) is a separate dedicated mode with pause-and-repeat drills across six regional accents: American, British, Australian, Argentina, Mexico, and Castilian.


Accent coverage differs structurally. Babbel builds separate tracks per language variant, so Spanish (Spain) and Spanish (Mexico) are distinct courses chosen at signup. ISSEN lets you switch regional accents inside the same language without starting a new track, useful if you want a Buenos Aires tutor one week and a Mexico City tutor the next.


## Languages supported


Babbel offers 14 languages, each built as a dedicated curriculum with scenario content and recorded dialogues. ISSEN covers 60+ languages for real-time voice tutoring, including less commonly taught ones where human conversation partners are hard to find locally, a point worth weighing against other[AI voice tutors](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-voice-tutors-language-learning/) on the market.

Babbel's smaller catalog reflects deep per-language production. ISSEN's wider catalog matters most if you are learning something like Finnish, Vietnamese, or Ukrainian and cannot easily find a tutor willing to meet three times a week, a gap also filled by several[Rosetta Stone alternatives](https://www.issen.com/blog/rosetta-stone-alternatives-ai-voice-tutor/) built for daily speaking.


## Pricing and plans


Babbel's individual plans, per its[pricing page](https://my.babbel.com/en/prices) , include a 12-month subscription at around $8.95 per month ($107.40 billed annually, with frequent 50% off promotions) and a Lifetime option at $299.99 covering all 14 languages. Following the Babbel Live shutdown, there is no human-tutor add-on for individual learners.


ISSEN runs on a flat monthly subscription in the $20 to $29 USD range depending on plan and region, with unlimited daily practice and a 10-minute free trial.

Cost-per-rep is the number that matters. Babbel's lower fee rewards learners finishing short lessons on a predictable cadence. ISSEN's flat price favors learners who want unlimited speaking reps, where a daily 20-minute session drives cost-per-conversation well below either plan. Human tutor marketplaces like Preply and italki run $15 to $40 per session, reasonable at one or two sessions a week but prohibitive at daily volume, which is part of why many learners compare[AI language tutors](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-language-tutors-conversation-practice/) for daily conversation practice instead.


## Who each app is best suited for


### Who Babbel fits


Babbel suits beginners and early intermediates in one of its 14 languages who want a defined syllabus and short daily lessons. If you are building vocabulary and grammar foundations from scratch, prefer 10 to 15 minute sessions with visible progress markers, and want scaffolded speaking practice through Babbel Speak's preset scenarios, the structure holds up well.


### Who ISSEN fits


ISSEN suits B1 and above learners whose passive knowledge outpaces what comes out of their mouth. You need speaking volume no weekly tutor can supply, you want to practice hands-free on a walk or commute, and you benefit from a tutor that remembers what you stumbled over last session and loops back to it.


If you are an absolute beginner, pair ISSEN with a syllabus-based app until you can hold a basic exchange, then let the conversation reps take over, a tradeoff worth weighing in any comparison of[AI vs. human tutors](https://www.issen.com/blog/ai-vs-human-tutor-language-speaking/) for speaking practice.


## Why ISSEN is the Better Choice for Speaking Practice


Babbel has earned its reputation. The curriculum is expert-built, the brand is trusted, the entry price is low, and Babbel Speak is a sensible first step for beginners who want guided scenarios before facing an open conversation, much like the gamified-versus-conversational tradeoff covered in the[ISSEN vs Duolingo comparison](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-app-speaking-issen-duolingo/) . If a structured syllabus is what you need right now, it holds up.


For learners whose goal is conversational fluency, ISSEN is the stronger fit. Voice-first design, real-time unpredictable exchanges, cross-session memory that loops back to what you stumbled over last week, a dedicated Shadowing mode for pronunciation drills, and background mode that turns a 20-minute walk into 20 minutes of speaking reps, the same strengths that show up in the[ISSEN vs Talkpal comparison](https://www.issen.com/blog/issen-talkpal-comparison/) . The next conversation you have with a real person is the thing that gets easier.


Start a 10-minute conversation with ISSEN and keep the daily reps going from there.


## Final thoughts on choosing a speaking-first alternative to Babbel


If you are early in a language and want structure, Babbel's syllabus holds up and the entry price is hard to argue with. Once you can read more than you can say out loud, the bottleneck is speaking volume, and that is where a real-time voice tutor earns its keep. Start a short conversation with[ISSEN](https://issen.com/) and build the habit from there.


## FAQ


### Should I pick Babbel or ISSEN if I'm an absolute beginner in a new language?


Babbel is the better starting point if you need a defined syllabus to build initial vocabulary and grammar in one of its 14 languages. Once you can hold a basic exchange, bring ISSEN in for daily speaking reps, since open conversation assumes you can produce something to work with.


### What's the core difference between Babbel Speak and ISSEN's open conversation mode?


Babbel Speak walks you through expert-written scenarios with scaffolded prompts, so you rehearse dialogues the app has prepared. ISSEN runs open-ended voice conversations with smart turn detection, real-time difficulty adjustment, and cross-session memory, so the exchange moves with what you say instead of following a preset script.


### Does Babbel still offer live human tutoring as a Babbel alternative for speaking?


No. Babbel Live, the group-class offering with human instructors, was discontinued on July 1, 2025. If you want human tutoring alongside app-based practice, Preply or italki remain the standard options for weekly sessions, with ISSEN handling the daily speaking volume in between.


### Is ISSEN worth the higher monthly price compared to Babbel?


It depends on cost-per-rep, not the sticker price. Babbel's ~$8.95/month annual plan is cheaper per month, but ISSEN's $20 to $29 flat fee with unlimited daily practice drops well below $1 per conversation if you run a 20-minute session each day, a volume Babbel's lesson-based structure isn't built to supply.


### Can ISSEN replace structured grammar study for languages like German or Japanese?


No, and that's not the design. ISSEN is one input inside a broader study plan that fills the speaking-reps gap apps, textbooks, and weekly tutors can't deliver at scale, while grammar instruction and vocabulary building still belong in your stack alongside it.
